column2: NOT PORTED, AND THE REASON IS ENGINEERING, NOT ATTRIBUTION
column3: cuVS shipping no GPU kd-tree is NOT the reason and must not be given as one. The reason is the structure: a kd-tree query is a per-query stack walk with data-dependent branching and per-lane divergent memory access, which is the shape a GPU is worst at, and above roughly 15 dimensions the pruning bound stops firing and it degenerates to a full scan -- so it would lose to the brute force in this directory on exactly the workloads it claims to help. The structure that DOES help in low dimensions is already here: cuVS's RANDOM BALL COVER (`impl/neighbors/ball_cover/`), exact, one level over sqrt(n) landmarks, no stack, no divergence, and it is what `RadiusNeighbors` already uses. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OWED is `rbc_knn_query` (the row below), not a tree

the k-NN (as opposed to eps/radius) query over the built RBC index. `impl/neighbors/ball_cover/` has the index BUILD and both eps paths; this is the missing third entry point and it is the real answer to "I want a spatial index instead of brute force" for low-dimensional data. cuML restricts the same index to <= 3 dimensions and to {euclidean, haversine, l2} (`nearest_neighbors.pyx:439-441`, `neighbors/__init__.py:49`), which is the honest scope
